transcript:
Meeting: Dev Sandbox Provisioning & SDK Bootstrapping
Date: 2025-02-11 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Evan Clarke (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (VerityDocs - Staff Eng); Carlos Ruiz (Platform Eng); Lina Park (PM)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python + TS), provisioning a dev sandbox, auth patterns (API keys, SSO/SAML questions), and a short run of a sample generation to validate env. Agreed to share sandbox guide, sample repo, and run a perf script on VerityDocs prompts.

Topics: SDK install, env variables, API keys vs SSO, VPC/onprem considerations, sample repo run, basic Optimize tips for cost control (batching, cache), next steps for pilot.

References shared: Sandbox guide (link): https://redwood-inference.docs/sandbox-provisioning-veritydocs ; Sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sandbox-sample ; Security pack (short): link shared in chat.

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan (Redwood): ok hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Evan, account exec, with Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya (VerityDocs): doing well thanks, Maya here. we just had a quick stand earlier — excited to get into the SDK bits.
[00:14] Priya (Redwood): hey, hi, hi. I'm Priya. i'll drive the quick lab steps and then we'll hit the sandbox provisioning flow.
[00:21] Carlos (VerityDocs): Carlos here, platform team. main thing for us is env parity and VPC stuff — and we need to check the allowlist/egress.
[00:29] Lina (VerityDocs): and i'm Lina, PM. we're tracking success metrics: latency under 300ms for interactive docs, cost under $X per 1k tokens, and secure handling of PII.
[00:40] Evan: great, i put the success criteria in the notes, good to be explicit. quick qual: what stacks are you using for app and infra?
[00:47] Maya: app is node/TS frontend, backend python fastapi running in k8s on GCP. we use GCS, and internal auth is okta.
[00:55] Priya: perfect. so for SDKs you'll be using both python and typescript examples, we have quickstart snippets for both. we'll demo the python flow and then show the TS variant.
[01:06] Priya: first step is provisioning a dev sandbox — we create a sandbox org for you and issue an API key scoped for dev, TTL 30 days by default, you can rotate keys via console.
[01:18] Carlos: question: can the sandbox be VPC peered or is it public with IP allowlist?
[01:23] Evan: good q — for hosted sandboxes we do IP allowlist and org-level allowlist by default. VPC peering is in Dedicated/Private tiers but we can provision a private trial if you need peering.
[01:36] Carlos: ok that might be needed for compliance, we have to check infra constraints.
[01:40] Maya: on auth, we want SSO for pilot. how does SAML map to the console?
[01:45] Priya: we support SAML/SSO for enterprise console access; for API access typical pattern is short-lived API keys issued after SSO exchange or a token broker. we can show the token-exchange flow in the follow-up.
[01:58] Lina: and audit logs — do you keep request-level logs? retention?
[02:02] Evan: yes, request logs with redaction options. retention tiers vary; we'll share the SOC2/security pack with specifics.
[02:10] Maya: cool. can we step through the python quickstart?
[02:13] Priya: yep, i'll share my screen, opening the sample repo.
[02:20] [screen share noise] Priya: ok repo at github.com/redwood-inference/sandbox-sample, we'll focus on sample_app/python/quickstart.py. first install pip package redwood-client (note: package name might change; see README).
[02:36] Priya: pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.2  — in the sample we show env var REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ORG.
[02:45] Priya: example snippet: client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); response = client.generate("summarize: ...") — slight paraphrase because of transcriber.
[02:58] Evan: common mistake is committing keys; we recommend using secrets manager + CI injector.
[03:04] Maya: yep, we use GCP secret manager. how do we pass keys in CI?
[03:08] Priya: we show a GitHub Actions example that pulls secret from GCP and sets REDWOOD_API_KEY env var for the workflow.
[03:15] Carlos: any examples for streaming in TS? our UI wants progressive tokens.
[03:19] Priya: yes, TS sample under sample_app/ts has both the streaming ws client and the fetch-based stream wrapper. streaming is via SSE in our hosted API.
[03:27] [crosstalk] Lina: and is there backpressure handling?
[03:30] Priya: we have examples with incremental UI updates and how to cancel requests — also show KV cache advice to speed repeated prompts.
[03:38] Maya: wait, is that KV cahce or KV cache?
[03:40] Evan: KV cache, caching the key-value attention cache for long-running chat sessions — but we can control TTLs.
[03:48] Priya: next i'll do a live run of a sample generation against the dev sandbox key that Evan created earlier.
[03:55] [sound of typing]
[04:02] Priya: ok running quickstart now, it should be a small summarize of a doc.
[04:07] [engine output noise]
[04:12] Priya: response comes back, latency ~210ms for the sample prompt, tokens 420. (note: these are demo numbers not benched).
[04:20] Carlos: nice. how do we control unit cost?
[04:23] Priya: primary levers: model selection (smaller models for drafts), batching for throughput jobs, prefix caching for repeated contexts, and quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize. we can suggest config for your workload.
[04:36] Maya: on quantization — do we have instructions for local inference or is that only in private?
[04:40] Priya: local/on-prem quantization workflows are part of Private offering; Optimize gives recommendations for hosted/dedicated quant profiles. will share notes.
[04:49] Lina: exceptional, ok can we see the console for sandbox keys?
[04:52] [screen changes] Priya: here's the org console, under API -> Keys. you can create scoped keys, set expirations, add IP allowlists.
[05:03] Maya: and role-based access? we want to restrict rotate-only versus full admin.
[05:06] Priya: yes RBAC roles: Viewer, Developer, Admin, Billing. you can also create custom roles in the enterprise plan.
[05:15] Carlos: one more on networking — egress to third-party telemetry? we need to vet where logs go.
[05:21] Evan: we redact by default and offer an audited routing option for enterprise — will include in security pack.
[05:27] [10 minutes of technical Q/A omitted in export for brevity but present in call]
[15:31] Priya: jumping ahead to SDK env best practices: 1) don't embed keys, 2) use short-lived keys in CI, 3) instrument token counts per route, 4) enable prefix caching for conversational UX.
[15:50] Maya: about token accounting — any dashboards for per-endpoint breakdown?
[15:54] Evan: Console > Usage shows per-route and per-model cost breakdown and token histograms. we can create a view for your routes if you want.
[16:03] Carlos: can we get trial credits for the sandbox so we can run the perf script?
[16:06] Evan: yes we can allocate trial credits; i'll attach to the new sandbox org.
[16:12] Lina: we need to run a perf test with 2k concurrent requests later to simulate spikes, will your dedicated offering give that predictable throughput?
[16:20] Priya: Dedicated gives predictable GPU pools and autoscaling policies. for spikes we can provision burst capacity or fallback routing to cheaper region/model to keep tail latency bounded.
[16:32] Maya: curious about fallback — if a model falls back does output format change? we need structured JSON outputs.
[16:38] Priya: good point — our automatic fallback tries to match model families; for strict schemas we recommend using function/tool calling or structured output validation in the app. we'll demo that in follow-up.
[16:51] Evan: quick note on privacy: data at rest encrypted by default, and key management hooks to customer KMS available in Private.
[17:00] Carlos: ok thanks. can you run a small bench now against our provided prompt set?
[17:04] Priya: we have their prompt set? Maya uploaded it to the shared drive earlier this morning?
[17:10] Maya: yes link in chat — it's a set of 150 doc-summary prompts.
[17:14] Priya: ok i'll kick off a small run (non-concurrent) now and share raw numbers after.
[17:19] [typing]
[17:27] Priya: quick aside — when you run local integration tests, set REDWOOD_ENV=dev to hit the sandbox endpoint.
[17:33] Evan: also note rate-limits differ between hosted sandbox and production dedicated. we'll add guidance in the sandbox doc.
[17:40] Lina: any gotchas with the TypeScript SDK versioning? we saw breaking changes in minor before.
[17:45] Priya: we maintain semver and publish changelogs; the sample repo pins minor ranges for stability. we recommend using a CI job to alert on SDK update PRs.
[17:55] Carlos: how about CORS and client-side keys for streaming?
[17:59] Priya: short-lived browser tokens via a token broker is the recommended pattern — don't embed long-lived keys in the frontend. we have an example auth broker in sample_app.
[18:10] Evan: ok bringing it back — next steps we'll: provision sandbox, Evan will drop links and credits, Priya will run perf script, VerityDocs will send final prompt set and token estimate.
[18:20] Maya: sounds good. any compliance docs you can share?
[18:23] Evan: yes SOC2, ISO, and the security whitepaper — link in chat, i'll email the full pack.
[18:28] Lina: timeline — we'd like a pilot in two weeks if possible.
[18:32] Evan: that aligns, we'll aim to have sandbox + perf by 2/18 so you can review before pilot start.
[18:40] Carlos: minor question — does Redwood Optimize automatically suggest batching or is that manual?
[18:44] Priya: Optimize provides recommended batching and quant settings based on observed token distributions; some suggestions are auto-applied for caching but heavier quant changes need ops acceptance.
[18:55] Maya: ok thanks super useful.
[19:00] [brief pause, screens shared for a few minutes with repo walkthrough]
[25:02] Priya: demo wrap-up — I've created a perf job entry and will run it overnight against the 150 prompts, then share results as a spreadsheet.
[25:15] Evan: i'll also open the sandbox org and add Maya and Carlos as Developers so they can generate keys.
[25:22] Maya: perfect, thanks.
[25:27] Lina: can we get a separate meeting for VPC/private options with infra stakeholders?
[25:31] Evan: yes let's tentatively book 60 min the week of 2/24 — i'll ping availability.
[25:40] Carlos: thanks all.
[25:42] Evan: cool — recap of next steps in chat and action items captured.
[25:47] Maya: thanks team.
[25:49] [meeting ends — autopause]
